items.title: my digital footprint is f*cked
items.summary:
my digital footprint is f*cked

i got early access to GPT-6 Cyber ​​and connected it to Grok Bot.

then i gave it my phone number, old usernames, email addresses, and one instruction:

“find every version of me that’s still out there.”

i expected abandoned accounts.

it found an address i moved out of years ago. a profile under a username i’d forgotten. my number attached to a company i no longer work for.

then Grok started connecting the records.

different websites. different names. the same person.

me.

Grok handled the search.
Cyber ​​investigated the weak points.
Grok used the openings to reach the databases and remove the matching records.

i was watching the terminal on my phone when the first profile disappeared.

refreshed the page.

gone.

another record. another lookup. another result that no longer focused on me.

the part that got me wasn’t the code flying across the screen.

it was searching my own number afterward and getting nothing useful back.

i’d spent years blocking individual spam callers while the same information kept getting passed around.

now the phone was quiet.

no “quick question.”
no recruiter asking about a job from three years ago.
no stranger who somehow already knew my name.

i kept checking whether my phone was on silent.

it wasn't.

for once, searching for me didn’t hand someone a map of my life.

items.summary:

it took me a week of researching polishing figuring out and becoming BETTER then the original 

and as promised im LEAKING the prompt for FREE 

he got 100M views in the past 30 days averaging 8M views per vid 

this style is a mix of a 2d character with a 3d background 

ive seen a few people try to recreate this but they dont end up like the og 

so how did i make this? 

-> Install Blender from their Website
-> run the installer 
-> paste the prompt in claude 
-> generate the script 
-> make a voiceover using the script 

and the rest is fully automated

chat gpt will build out the scenes in blender using a python script  and sends a Windows Batch file ( .bat ) to a folder you specify 

u just simply double click the Render .bat file no need to even open blender 

blender will create the full video on your gpu , rendering times depend on your GPU cores the TI series GPU's have a faster render time 1.5-3sec per frame 

this video in particular was 1900 frames and took me 1.5 hours to render on my GPU 

anyways here is the free prompt thank me later ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for my story, or pitch 3.
- A good one is true and little known. Someone does something that looks ridiculous, someone laughs at them, and the reveal flips who was smart: a trick, a scheme, a bluff, a loophole, revenge.
- Give each pitch with its first line, the mocker, the twist, and a title that hides the ending.
Ask which voice I want:
- Free, the default: Kokoro, run locally on the CPU.
- Optional upgrade: ElevenLabs with a stock library voice. Tell me the credit cost before you generate anything, and make one take.
Ask what GPU I have. Any GPU works: Blender EEVEE renders on all of them, just slower on older cards.
Tell me everything else is free: Blender, Python, Playwright with a headless browser, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, Pixabay music and Mixkit sound effects. No image, video or 3D model generator is used anywhere.
Then write the script and the beat list with seconds, and show me both before you build anything.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 1080x1920, 30 fps, 55-70 s vertical Short in the style of narrated "true story with a twist" cartoon Shorts: flat 2D cartoon people acting inside lit, dressed 3D toon sets, one storyteller voice, captions of 1-2 words, and one camera that keeps travelling.

Sets (Blender, built by a Python script):
- Build every place in the story from simple shapes in code (boxes, cylinders, cones, tori, bevelled boxes), never a downloaded model.
- Materials: flat toon colours with low roughness, so it reads like a cartoon, not a photo.
- Ink outlines: an inverted-hull shell on every object (a Solidify modifier with flipped normals and a dark backface-only material), so the world has the same line as the characters.
- Draw surfaces on a canvas and use them as textures: signs, chalkboards, brick, planks, plaques.
- Put the story's words inside the world (signs, boards, counters) instead of floating titles.
Palette and light:
- Pick a warm key against cool shadows for each place. Balance cream, ochre and amber against blue, teal and purple.
- Costumes contrast with the set.
- Interiors: warm practical lamps plus a soft cool fill. Exteriors: a strong sun, a blue sky and a lighter horizon.
- Render with EEVEE, the Standard view transform, a slight lowered exposure, and a soft glow added in the finish.
People:
- 2D characters are drawn in code (HTML canvas) and exported as transparent images, one per pose and expression. In Blender they sit on camera-facing cards that turn around the vertical axis only.
- Use an emission material on the cards so faces stay clean white whatever the lighting.
- The look, kept simple:
  - a big round white head with a thick dark brush outline
  - big expressive eyes and brows, a small nose, a mouth that changes shape
  - thin stick legs and chunky flat-colour clothes
  - one signature prop or accessory each (glasses, a hat, a cigar, a tool)
- The face set: smug, grin, shock, laughing, worried, sweat drops.
- Pose-to-pose acting: point, hold up a prop, hands on hips, arms up. Blinks and small breathing keep holds alive.
- A new, original cast for every video. Show me a character sheet before building.
Camera:
- One camera that travels between beats. Each beat holds with a slow push, then the camera moves to the next.
- Fit every camera key to what it should show: compute the distance so the named faces or props sit fully in frame.
- Inserts carry the proof: a close-up on the key object while the change happens.
- The payoff is the biggest frame in the video: a reveal coming at the lens.
- Soft dissolves or camera moves between places, few hard cuts.
Captions:
- 1-2 words at a time; short words (a, the, so, to) ride with the next word.
- A bold rounded font, white with a thick dark outline, centred in the lower third.
- No full stops on screen.
Banned:
- AI images or video, downloaded 3D models, real logos
- a camera that sits still
- half-cut faces, legs-only or hat-only frames, empty backgrounds
- a time-stretched or whispered voice
- more than one or two names the viewer has to remember
</direction>

<structure>
Length: 55-70 s, about 150-200 words.
Beat map for a 62 s Short (scale it to your voice):
0-4 s, HOOK: one plain sentence about an act that makes no sense, with the reason hidden. Picture it in one frame.
4-12 s, SETUP: who, where, and what's at stake, with one exact number.
12-20 s, THE MOCKER: a quoted joke line said to the hero. Big close-up.
20-40 s, THE METHOD: it gets weirder in steps. One close-up insert per step.
40-50 s, "YOU SEE,": the trick explained through an everyday thing the viewer has done.
50-62 s, THE PAYOFF and THE TWIST: shown, not explained. The last line is the biggest reveal and calls back to the hook.
</structure>

<build>
1. Tools (all free): Blender (any recent version), Python 3, Node with Playwright, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, numpy. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Script:
   - Tell it the way a kid tells a friend: plain words, sentences joined with "and" and "so", one funny comparison, no dates or jargon.
   - Join related sentences with commas, because a voice resets after every full stop and leaves a gap.
   - Show me the word count and the seconds per line.
3. Voice:
   - Free route: Kokoro on the CPU, one line per call, joined with short gaps.
   - Paid route: ElevenLabs, one take, cost stated first.
   - Only trim silence, never inside a word. Then run faster-whisper on the finished track to get word times.
4. Characters: draw the cast in code, show me a sheet, then export every pose/expression the story needs as transparent WebP.
5. Story timeline: one file that, for any frame, returns the camera (position, look-at, fov, roll), the focus distance, and each character's card, position and scale. Anchor every beat and sound to a word time, never a typed time.
6. Exporter: a headless browser page runs the timeline for every frame and writes frames.json plus the card images and sign textures.
7. Blender scene script (blender -b -P https://t.co/TnwLWonFx3 -- --data data --out frames):
   - builds every set, light and prop
   - reads frames.json, places the camera and cards each frame, animates the props
   - renders JPG frames, skips frames that already exist so it can resume
8. Contact sheet before the full render: stills from the middle of every shot, labelled with time and the line being spoken. I approve or ask for changes.
9. Sound:
   - Music: one playful bed under a free licence, about 20 dB under the voice.
   - Effects: real Mixkit sounds placed on the actions (whooshes on camera travels, pops on reveals, impacts, dings).
   - Duck music and effects under speech. Normalise to -14 LUFS.
10. Finish with FFmpeg: a soft glow (screen-blend a blurred highlight pass at about 0.4 opacity), burned-in captions, the mix, H.264.
11. Give me a one-click .bat (or .sh) that runs the export, the Blender render and the finish. It must refuse to encode if any frame is missing, and never overwrite an older video.
12. Upload text:
   - Title: "The [thing] That [strange act]", hiding the ending.
   - Cover: a clean frame of the payoff with no text.
</build>

<gotchas>
Script:
- Scripts that read like writing (names, dates, context, the twist in the hook) fall flat. Line 1 is the strange act with the reason hidden.
Voice:
- Short full-stop sentences make the voice stop-start. Join lines with commas.
- Trimming at whisper timestamps clips words. Trim on silence only, with a small guard.
Look:
- Empty sets read as cheap. Dress every place with props and background detail.
- Characters scaled too small look like kids next to tables. Scale them so they stand about 1.9 m against the real-size sets.
Camera:
- Hand-placed cameras crop faces at 9:16; the frame is narrow. Fit keys to the subjects and scan every frame for cut faces before rendering.
- A camera that flies through a wall, a canopy or a post reads as a glitch. Pick another angle or cut.
Render:
- 3D props attached to a 2D card must follow the card's turn, or they drift off the drawn body.
- A render that stops early (sleep, crash) must not be encoded into a short video. Check the frame count first.
- Turn off PC sleep before a long render.
Sound:
- Music only a few dB under the voice makes the narrator hard to hear. Keep it low and measure.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my story, or pitch 3. Then show me the script (word count and seconds per line) and the beat list before any voice is generated or any scene is built.
</start>

Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
